title: ONGC Interim Dividend 2026: What Investors Need to Know
description: ONGC's board announced an interim dividend of 160% after its Q2 FY27 results on November 5. This translates to a dividend payout of ₹8 per equity share, based.

faq.a: An interim dividend is a dividend paid by a company to its shareholders before the company's full annual earnings have been determined and before the Annual General Meeting (AGM). It's often declared when a company has strong half-yearly or quarterly profits.

The ex-dividend date is the day on or after which a stock trades without its dividend benefit. If you buy a stock on or after the ex-dividend date, you will not be eligible to receive the recently declared dividend.

The record date is the specific date on which a company determines which shareholders are eligible to receive the dividend. To be included in the list of eligible shareholders, your name must appear in the company's records by the end of this date.

faq.q: How are dividends taxed in India for resident individuals?
faq.a: Dividends received from Indian companies are taxable in the hands of the shareholder at their applicable income tax slab rates. If the dividend exceeds ₹5,000 in a financial year, the company will deduct 10% TDS.

faq.q: Do NRIs pay tax on dividends in India?
faq.a: Yes, NRIs also pay tax on dividends received from Indian companies. TDS is typically deducted at 20% (plus surcharge and cess), though this rate can be lower if specified by a Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement (DTAA).

faq.q: When can I expect the dividend payment?
faq.a: Typically, dividend payments are processed within 30 days of the declaration date, but the exact payment date is usually announced by the company along with the record date.
